ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC=20\,cm$, $DE$ is perpendicular bisector of $AB$ with the foot of the perpendicular as $E$, and intersects $AC$ at $D$. If $BC=15\,cm$, then what is the perimeter of $\triangle DBC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $DE$ bisects $AB$ perpendicularly,\\
it follows that $AD=BD$,\\
hence the perimeter of $\triangle DBC = BD+DC+BC = AD+DC+BC = AC+BC$,\\
since $AB=AC=20\,cm$, $BC=15\,cm$,\\
therefore, the perimeter of $\triangle DBC =AC+BC=20+15=\boxed{35}\,cm$.

Reasoning: The problem states that DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB, so any point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from the two points A and B. D is on DE, so DA=DB.
